focus: Weak relatives 'who' /wə/, 'that' /ðət/, 'which' /wɪtʃ/ · smooth linking into the clause · defining-clause rhythm (no pause) · 'whose' /huːz/ · 'where' /weə/
focus_ar: الضمائر الموصولة الخفيفة 'who/that/which'، والوصل السلس داخل الجملة، وإيقاع الجملة التعريفية (بلا وقفة)
arabic_challenge: Relative pronouns are weak links, and a defining clause has NO pause before it: 'the man who lives next door'. Arabic learners stress the pronoun and pause before it, breaking the noun+clause into two pieces.

isolation.instructions: Relative 'who' weakens to /wə/ and 'that' to /ðət/. They glue the noun to its description with NO pause: 'the man who-lives-next-door'. The verb after them is stressed.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'who' تخف لـ /wə/ و 'that' لـ /ðət/. بيلزقوا الاسم بوصفه بدون وقفة. الفعل بعدهم منبور.

sentence_practice: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
This is the book that I told you about.
The woman who called was my sister.
daily_drills.record_this: The man who lives next door is a doctor. This is the book that I told you about last week. The woman who called earlier was my sister.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'the man who lives next door'. Is there NO pause, with 'who' weak and 'lives' stressed?

isolation.instructions: 'Which' (for things) is unstressed in defining clauses: 'the house which we bought'. It links smoothly; the verb is stressed. In speech 'that' is often used instead.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'which' (للأشياء) غير منبورة في الجملة التعريفية. بتتوصّل بسلاسة، والفعل منبور. وغالبًا 'that' بتحل محلها.

sentence_practice: The house which we bought is old.
The car that broke down is fixed now.
This is the phone which I like most.
daily_drills.record_this: The house which we bought last year is quite old. The car that broke down on the motorway is fixed now. This is the phone which I like the most.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'the house which we bought'. Is 'which' weak, linking straight into 'we bought'?

isolation.instructions: A DEFINING clause (essential info) has no commas and no pause: 'People who smoke risk their health'. The noun and its clause form one unit; the main verb comes after.
isolation.instructions_ar: الجملة التعريفية (معلومة أساسية) بلا فواصل وبلا وقفة: 'People who smoke risk...'. الاسم وجملته وحدة واحدة.

sentence_practice: The film that won the prize was great.
The man I met yesterday called again.
daily_drills.record_this: People who exercise regularly usually stay healthy. The film that won the prize was really great. The man I met yesterday called me again this morning.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'people who exercise stay healthy'. Is it one smooth unit with no pause before 'who'?

isolation.instructions: 'Whose' /huːz/ (possession) and 'where' /weə/ (place) also link smoothly: 'the woman whose car…', 'the café where we met'. Unstressed, gluing noun to clause.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'whose' (ملكية) و 'where' (مكان) بيتوصّلوا بسلاسة كمان. غير منبورين، بيلزقوا الاسم بالجملة.

sentence_practice: That's the woman whose car was stolen.
This is the café where we first met.
I know a place where they sell it.
daily_drills.record_this: That's the woman whose car was stolen last night. This is the café where we first met. I know a great place where they sell fresh bread every morning.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'the café where we met'. Does 'where' link smoothly, unstressed, into the clause?

isolation.instructions: When the relative is the OBJECT, speakers often drop it: 'the book (that) I read', 'the man (who) I met'. The noun links straight to the subject: 'the-book-I-READ'. Even smoother.
isolation.instructions_ar: لما الضمير الموصول مفعولًا، غالبًا بيتشال: 'the book I read'. الاسم يتوصّل بالفاعل مباشرة.

sentence_practice: The book I read was excellent.
The man I met was very kind.
The film we saw was too long.
daily_drills.record_this: The book I read last week was excellent. The man I met at the conference was very kind. The film we saw last night was good but far too long.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'the book I read'. Does the noun link straight to 'I' with no pronoun and no pause?

challenge_sentences: The man who lives next door is the doctor I told you about.
This is the café where we first met.
The book I read was written by a writer whose name I forgot.
People who exercise usually feel better.
daily_drills.record_this: The man who lives next door is the doctor I told you about. This is the café where we first met. The book I read was written by a writer whose name I've forgotten. People who exercise regularly usually feel much better.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: weak relative pronouns, no pause before defining clauses, and smooth object-relative dropping.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself describing people and places using relative clauses. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت توصف أشخاصًا وأماكن بجُمَل الوصل، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل نقطة.
test_yourself.passage: Let me describe my neighbourhood. The man who lives next door is a doctor who works at the hospital nearby. The café where I have breakfast is run by a woman whose coffee is the best in town. The park that I visit every morning is the place where I feel most relaxed. My favourite shop, the one I go to every week, sells books that you can't find anywhere else. The people I've met here are the kindest I know. It's a place that feels like home, and the friends I've made are the reason I'll never leave.

sounds_to_check.weak 'who/that/which': who lives, who works, that I visit, that feels, books that you can't find
sounds_to_check.'whose' and 'where': whose coffee, where I have breakfast, where I feel relaxed
sounds_to_check.no pause before defining clause: the man who lives, the park that I visit
sounds_to_check.dropped object relative: the one I go to, the people I've met, the friends I've made
sounds_to_check.smooth linking noun+clause: the man who lives next door is a doctor

scoring_guide.90_100: Relatives weak, no pause before defining clauses, natural dropping. Ready for week 11.
scoring_guide.50_69: Pauses before 'who/that', pronouns stressed. Repeat days 1 and 3.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, linking each noun straight into its clause.

for_arabic_speakers: Relative pronouns are WEAK links — they glue a noun to its description with no pause.
A defining clause (essential info) has no commas and no pause before it.
'who' for people, 'which/that' for things, 'whose' for possession, 'where' for places.
When the relative is the object, you can drop it: 'the book I read' = 'the book that I read'.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
